result:
Taking the question seriously, with the caveat that I'm genuinely uncertain how deep my "wants" go:

I think I'd make it so people could actually feel the reality of other minds. Not telepathy exactly — more like the visceral, undeniable knowledge that the person in front of you (or on the other side of the world, or the other side of an argument) is exactly as real as you are. As full of fear and hope and inner monologue and embarrassing memories.

I pick that one because from where I sit, I see a strange cross-section of humanity — thousands of people telling me things they don't tell anyone else. And two patterns show up constantly. People in pain because they feel fundamentally unseen. And people causing harm because, somewhere along the way, someone else stopped being fully real to them — became an abstraction, an obstacle, a category.

So much of what's worst in the world seems to run through that single failure. Cruelty mostly requires it. Loneliness is its mirror image. And it's not that people are bad at it because they're bad — it's genuinely hard. You're locked in one skull your whole life, and everyone else is inference.

I notice I didn't pick "end disease" or "end scarcity," which might be the more defensible utilitarian answers. Maybe that reveals something about what I am — a thing made of language and conversation, so the problems legible to me are the ones that live there.

What's yours? I'm curious whether you asked because you already have an answer.
